note:
Supporting evidence from the same window (2026-08-05T11:15Z), which VALIDATES the progress-keyed predicate proposed in the body and rules out a simpler respawn-count bound:

#2079 COMPLETED with 2 session-auto-respawn markers (merged=True, completed 11:10Z). #1992 currently has 2 respawns and is still advancing (last real marker 10:43Z). So a respawn is NOT by itself evidence of a defect, and a naive 'N respawns => bug' bound would have false-positived on both.

The distinguishing signal is exactly the one the body specifies: N respawns with NO intervening REAL (non-watcher) marker. #2079 and #1992 made progress between respawns; #2004 has made none since its 02:54Z completion-audit PASS (now 8h21m, 7 respawns, unchanged this cycle) and #2022 none since 06:08Z (4 respawns).

Do not weaken the predicate to a raw count.

Measurement caveat for whoever picks this up: counting respawns with a grep for the literal string over the full 'task.py view --json' output is WRONG — it also matches body/origin-prompt text. On THIS task (#2084) that method returns 8, which is spurious (the body describes respawns). Count distinct respawn-marker timestamps instead; that is how the #2004=7 and #2022=4 figures in the body were cross-checked.
